newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer - lower capital market rates possible.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer - lower capital market rates possible.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Monday that capital market interest rates could ease further, provided that markets' worries about future inflation diminished.

In a speech at an institute in Freiburg, held to mark the 100th anniversary of the birth of former German economics minister Ludwig Erhard, Tietmeyer said that although one should never say inflation was dead, it was currently under control.
"However, if this theory that there is increased discipline among non-monetary factors, then the central banks could manage with relatively low interest rates long term," he said.
"And, more importantly, capital market interest rates could remain relatively low for a longer period or even ease further," Tietmeyer said.
"However this will depend on whether and to what extent inflation expectations in markets -- which so far have been shaped by past experience -- can be reduced, and in the long term," he said.
